newsitem.title: UK: IGC raises 1996 world coarse grains crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: IGC raises 1996 world coarse grains crop estimate.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday raised its estimate for 1996 world coarse grains production to 889 million tonnes from its previous estimate of 884 million made a month ago.

The biggest factors in the rise were output increases for the former Yugoslavia and Russia. In its latest monthly report the IGC put coarse grains production in former Yugoslavia at 8.7 million tonnes compared to the previous estimate of 5.7 million and raised its estimate for Russia's crop to 33.9 million tonnes from the previous 31.8 million.
There was also a rise for Brazil to 34.7 million tonnes from 33.9 million and for Ethiopia by two million tonnes to 6.6 million.

The rises were offset by a series of cuts, including a reduction to 3.6 million tonnes from 4.7 million for Kazakhstan and from 10 million tonnes to 8.7 million for the CIS, not including Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan. South Africa's production was sen at 8.2 million tonnes from the previous estimate of 8.7 million.

The overall rise in estimated production overwhelmingly comes from maize, estimated at 574.2 million tonnes from the previous 571.2 million. It also saw a sharp rise in estimated sorghum production to 65.7 million tonnes from the previous 64.2 million.
The IGC put 1995 total world coarse grains output at 798 million tonnes.
